appraisal_events.evidence: la famille de Robert... en voulait à mort à M. de Borodino qui avait donné la permission pour Bruges... l'accusait de favoriser une liaison infâme. C'est quelqu'un de très mal... son expression de sévérité froncée envers l'horrible capitaine, dont elle dit avec une emphase ironique le nom: le Prince de Borodino, en femme pour qui l'Empire ne compte pas.
appraisal_events.explanation: Borodino is blamed for enabling Robert's disreputable liaison and simultaneously mocked by Mme de Villeparisis's ironic emphasis on his Napoleonic princely title, which counts for nothing to an old-regime Guermantes.

appraisal_events.evidence: J'aime beaucoup de Saint-Loup-en-Bray... parce qu'il est extrêmement bien élevé... j'ai appris quelques jours après que le jeune homme était le fils de Sir Rufus Israël! La fin de cette histoire parut moins choquante que son début, car elle resta incompréhensible... Sir Rufus Israël... était... un étranger parvenu, toléré par le monde... avec cette énergie affirmative, cet accent d'enthousiasme qu'on n'apporte qu'aux convictions qu'on ne s'est pas formées soi-même.
appraisal_events.explanation: Bloch's anecdote, meant to showcase Saint-Loup's admirable modesty toward a supposedly important personage, collapses because his premise about Sir Rufus Israël's prestige is wrong in Guermantes circles; the narrator exposes Bloch's naive, borrowed enthusiasm and social misjudgment.

status_effects.explanation: He is held responsible for enabling Robert's disreputable liaison, drawing open family resentment.
Mme de Villeparisis's ironic emphasis on his 'Prince' title, as someone for whom the Empire's nobility does not count, treats his rank as illegitimate or lesser before old aristocracy.
His attempt to impress the company with an anecdote about Saint-Loup's modesty backfires, exposing his misplaced values and second-hand, unexamined convictions.
His supposedly impressive anecdote lands as incomprehensible to his audience, undercutting his rhetorical performance.
Though Bloch reveres him as almost royal, the Guermantes milieu instead regards him as a merely tolerated foreign parvenu, undercutting Bloch's assumption within the same movement.

ambiguities: The blame directed at Borodino blends a parenthetical report of Robert's family's resentment with Mme de Villeparisis's own immediate ironic performance for the narrator, so it is not fully certain how much of the disapproval is her personal view versus relayed family sentiment.
